headline: Couch Crisis: Congress Orders Forensic Audit of 14 Empty Couches Following Routine Mall Inspection
deck: FBI Deploys Change-Sniffing Dogs to Strip Mall Parking Lots Amid National Panic Over Missing Upholstered Contents
article:
What started as a standard walk-through at Sunnyvale Mall in Nebraska has ballooned into a congressional order for a nationwide forensic audit of fourteen suspiciously vacant couches. Senator Gordon T. Quibble (R-NE) framed the effort as a matter of public accounting: "If these couches are just lying there collecting dust, who knows what else is being hidden in the upholstery? The American people deserve answers—preferably in round numbers."

HUD has sent FBI change-sniffing dogs to forty-seven strip-mall lots. The dogs are expected to locate stray fluff faster than human agents. The Pentagon has shifted $2.3 billion from missile programs to lint-trap satellites, a reallocation that defense analysts view as creative budgeting rather than strategic necessity.

The Round-Dollar Pricing Law now requires quarterly couch certification forms from every homeowners association. These filings will feed a national couch-filling index meant to measure neighborhood stability through upholstery volume. HOA chair Gladys P. Holdtight welcomed the paperwork: "An empty couch is just a gateway to other, darker secrets."

The National Bureau of Couch Investigations anticipates preliminary findings in weeks. One internal memo already floats the possibility that the couches simply arrived empty, a theory that has not yet slowed the audit schedule.
author: Patricia F. Duvall, Senior Staff Writer

weather.condition: Couches now officially classified as air

oped.title: Couch Voids Demand Total Furniture Scrutiny
oped.author: Dr. Reginald Cushionforth, Emeritus Chair of Round-Number Economics at the Institute for Mall Stability
oped.body: Fourteen empty couches reveal a preparedness gap that round pricing alone cannot fix. Any upholstered gap now counts as a potential decimal breach. The audit is the least disruptive option available. Shoppers who wear oversized hats that obstruct quick visual checks bear some responsibility for the current backlog. My own sectional, purchased at a reassuring $2,400, has never held so much as a nickel, yet the mall findings suggest others may still harbor fractional sympathies. Transparent furniture and a retail hat ban would close the loophole without further satellite spending.

classifieds.text: Empty sectional couch, $800 round. Post-FBI audit, zero change inside per new national rules. Desperate seller, couch must go before next mall sweep.
Seeking forensic couch auditors for Strip Mall chain. $20,000 per empty-furniture report, must tolerate change-sniffing dogs. Start yesterday.
Lost: Any hope of finding loose change in public seating. Found: fourteen fully audited, totally vacant couches. Reward: exactly $0.
Public Notice: Mall management apologizes for the empty-couch panic. All future furniture will be pre-cleared with round pricing only. No refunds on nothing.

panels.caption: Congressional aide: "These 14 couches flagged in the mall sweep contain zero contents. Launch the forensic audit."
FBI handler: "Deploy the change-sniffing dogs to every strip-mall lot. National security demands it."
Dog handler, radio crackling: "Negative findings. Couches were always empty. No pennies to begin with."

stories.headline: Change-Sniffing Dogs Cite Three Drivers for Concealing Canadian Quarters
stories.deck: Federal teams link glove-box hoards to broader upholstery shortfall
stories.article: After the mall sweeps, agents moved to interstate rest stops when metallic traces showed up on dashboards. Drivers described the quarters as toll-road souvenirs; investigators recorded them as unreported coin migration. Three citations followed under an emergency treasury rule against foreign small currency. Motorists signed affidavits promising no further change and accepted random future stops.

stories.headline: Furniture Retailers Report Record Returns of Sectionals Lacking Hidden Compartments
stories.deck: Buyers demand refunds after discovering standard empty interiors
stories.article: Retailers are fielding returns from buyers who expected loose coins beneath cushions. Every model has shipped empty since the shift to whole-dollar pricing. Disclosure tags now state that each piece contains only foam and fabric. Outlets have added a twenty-dollar restocking fee for the added inspection work.

stories.headline: National Lab Confirms Couch Fibers Contain No Trace Elements of Currency
stories.deck: Researchers map decade-long absence of metallic deposits in household seating
stories.article: Tests on upholstery from two hundred homes across six states found no copper or zinc particles. Researchers trace the absence to the 1792 decision against minting the penny. The report advises households to skip cushion checks during cleaning. Results match earlier examinations of bus seats and theater rows.

real_world_echo: Mysterious deaths of 14 elephants in Kenya prompts urgent inquiry, mirrored by treating the emptiness of exactly 14 couches as a baffling national mystery requiring urgent inquiry
